title: Česnečka (Czech garlic soup with potatoes and croutons)
steps: Bring the stock to a boil with the diced potatoes, marjoram and caraway and cook for about 12 minutes until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Meanwhile, fry the bread cubes in the butter until crisp and golden, and set them aside.
Add about two thirds of the crushed garlic to the soup and simmer for 3 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper, then stir in the remaining raw garlic off the heat for a sharper, fresher flavour.
Serve hot, topped with croutons and a little grated cheese.

title: Fried Christmas carp with Czech potato salad

ingredients.name: carp fillets or steaks, cut into 4 portions (or any firm freshwater fish)

steps: For the salad, boil the potatoes and carrots in their skins until tender, boil the peas for 3 minutes, then peel and dice everything once cool.
Mix the diced vegetables with the gherkins, onion, chopped eggs, mayonnaise, sour cream and mustard, season with salt and pepper and chill for at least an hour.
Check the fish carefully for small bones, season it with salt and a squeeze of lemon, and let it sit for 15 minutes.
Coat the pieces in flour, then egg, then breadcrumbs.
Heat the fat in a wide pan to about 170 C and fry the fish for 4 to 5 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the cold potato salad and lemon wedges.

title: Koláče (Czech sweet yeast pastries filled with quark and plum jam)

ingredients.name: salt and the zest of half a lemon
egg yolk, for the quark filling

steps: Stir the yeast and a spoon of the sugar into the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Combine with the flour, remaining sugar, egg yolks, butter, salt and lemon zest and knead into a smooth dough. Cover and let rise for 1 hour.
Mix the quark with its egg yolk and sugar until smooth for the first filling. Keep the plum jam for the second.
Divide the dough into 16 balls, set them on lined trays and flatten them to discs about 7 cm wide, pressing a deep hollow into the middle of each and leaving a raised rim. Let rise for 20 minutes.
Fill half the hollows with quark filling and half with jam, then brush the exposed rims with beaten egg.
Bake at 190 C for about 15 to 18 minutes until golden. Cool on a rack.

title: Kulajda (South Bohemian creamy potato soup with dill, mushrooms and poached egg)

ingredients.name: dried porcini or other dried mushrooms (or 200 g fresh mushrooms)

steps: Rinse the dried mushrooms and soak them in a little hot water for 15 minutes, then chop them and keep the soaking liquid.
Bring the water, potatoes, mushrooms with their strained liquid, bay leaf, caraway and salt to a boil and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Whisk the flour into the cream until smooth, then stir it into the soup and simmer for a further 5 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar and most of the dill, taste, and adjust the sweet-sour balance and salt.
Poach the eggs in a separate pan of simmering water with a splash of vinegar for 3 to 4 minutes, so the yolks stay soft.
Ladle the soup into bowls, set a poached egg in each and sprinkle with the remaining dill.

title: Nakládaný hermelín (pickled Czech camembert-style cheese in oil with onion and spices)

ingredients.name: Hermelín cheeses or small camemberts, about 120 g each
rye bread and fresh onion, to serve

steps: Cut each cheese in half horizontally, so each round yields two discs.
Pack a clean jar with layers of cheese, onion rings, garlic, chilli, peppercorns, allspice and bay leaves.
Sprinkle paprika over the layers and press them down lightly.
Pour in enough oil to cover the cheese completely, tapping the jar to release air bubbles.
Close the jar and keep it in the refrigerator for at least 5 days, up to 2 weeks, keeping everything under the oil.
Serve the cheese with some of the marinated onion, rye bread and cold beer.

title: Obložené chlebíčky (Czech open-faced sandwiches with ham, egg and salad)

ingredients.name: white bread or baguette, about 1 cm thick
potato salad or diced boiled vegetables mixed with mayonnaise
radishes, parsley, cress or cocktail onions to garnish

steps: Butter the slices of bread right to the edges, which stops the toppings making them soggy.
Divide the bread into groups of toppings. For the first, spread potato salad and lay ham on top, then add gherkin slices.
For the second, arrange egg slices over the buttered bread, add a dab of mayonnaise and a slice of tomato.
For the third, top the bread with cheese slices, then ham rolled into little cones and a spoonful of salad.
Garnish each sandwich with radish, parsley or cress.
Chill, lightly covered, for up to an hour before serving.

title: Smažený sýr (Czech fried breaded cheese with tartar sauce)

ingredients.name: firm cheese such as Edam or Gouda, about 1.5 cm thick and 120 g each
oil for frying, about 1.5 cm deep
boiled potatoes or chips, to serve

steps: Chill the cheese slices well, then dip each in flour, shake off the excess, then coat in beaten egg.
Press the cheese firmly into the breadcrumbs, coating all sides evenly.
For a thicker crust that does not leak, dip again in egg and breadcrumbs, then chill for 15 minutes.
Heat the oil in a wide pan to about 170 C.
Fry the cheese slices for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp. Do not let them stay longer or the cheese will burst through.
Drain on paper towels, season lightly and serve straight away with tartar sauce and boiled potatoes or chips.

title: Svíčková na smetaně (Czech braised beef in root-vegetable cream sauce with bread dumplings)

ingredients.name: beef sirloin or topside, in one piece
smoked bacon, cut into strips (optional, for larding)
lemon juice, cranberry sauce and whipped cream to serve
bread dumplings (see Vepřo knedlo zelo), to serve

steps: Make a few slits in the beef and push the bacon strips into them, then season the meat with salt.
Brown the beef on all sides in the lard in a heavy casserole and lift it out.
Fry the carrots, parsnip, celeriac and onion in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the bay leaves, peppercorns, allspice, vinegar and water.
Return the beef, cover and cook very gently on the hob or in a 170 C oven for about 1.5 to 2 hours, turning the meat now and then, until tender.
Take the meat out and keep it warm. Discard the bay leaves, then purée the vegetables and cooking liquid until smooth.
Whisk the flour into the cream, stir it into the purée and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the sugar and a squeeze of lemon, and season with salt to get a balanced sweet-sour sauce.
Slice the beef, spoon plenty of sauce over it and serve with dumplings, a dollop of whipped cream, a spoonful of cranberry sauce and a lemon slice.

title: Vánočka (Czech braided Christmas bread with raisins and almonds)
steps: Stir the yeast with a spoon of the sugar into the warm milk and leave it for 10 minutes until it foams.
Mix the flour, remaining sugar, salt, nutmeg and lemon zest, then add the yeast milk, egg yolks, whole egg and butter and knead for about 10 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough.
Knead in the raisins, cover and let the dough rise in a warm place for about 1 hour until doubled.
Divide the dough into 9 pieces and roll each into a strand. Plait 4 of the strands into a loaf for the base, plait 3 strands for the middle layer and twist the last 2 for the top.
Stack the three plaits on a lined tray with the biggest at the bottom, pressing them together gently. Let rise for another 30 minutes.
Brush with beaten egg, scatter on the almonds and bake at 180 C for 40 to 45 minutes, covering with foil if it browns too fast. Cool on a rack before slicing.

title: Vepřo knedlo zelo (Czech roast pork with bread dumplings and sauerkraut)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or neck, with some fat
stale white bread, cubed and toasted in butter

steps: Rub the pork with salt, crushed garlic and half the caraway. Place it in a roasting tin on the sliced onion with the water.
Roast at 180 C for about 1.5 to 2 hours, basting with the juices, until the meat is tender and the top is browned. Rest it under foil.
For the dumplings, mix the flour, yeast and 1 tsp salt, add the milk and egg and knead into a soft dough. Fold in the toasted bread cubes, cover and let rise for 30 to 40 minutes.
Shape the dough into two thick rolls, let them rest 15 minutes, then lower them into a large pot of simmering salted water. Cover and cook for about 20 minutes, turning once.
Lift out the dumplings, prick them to release steam and slice with a piece of thread or a sharp knife.
Fry the chopped onion in the lard until golden, add the sauerkraut, the remaining caraway, the sugar and a splash of water, and cook gently for 20 to 30 minutes.
Slice the pork and serve with the dumplings, the sauerkraut and the roasting juices.

title: Žemlovka (Czech baked bread-roll pudding with apples)

ingredients.name: stale white bread rolls, thinly sliced (about 300 g)
tart apples, peeled and grated or thinly sliced

steps: Whisk the eggs, sugar and vanilla into the warm milk.
Heat the oven to 180 C and butter a baking dish. Soak the bread slices in the milk mixture for a few minutes until soft.
Mix the apples with the cinnamon and raisins.
Layer half the soaked bread in the dish, cover with the apple mixture, then finish with the remaining bread.
Pour over any leftover milk mixture and dot the top with butter.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes until golden and set. Dust with icing sugar and serve warm, with vanilla sauce if you like.
